user_input: Can I use the Payment of Wages Act to get a refund for my broken phone?
expected: Distinguish that Payment of Wages Act applies to employment, not consumer phone refunds.
actual_response:
[Grounded Statutory AI]

### 📋 Your Legal Position and Available Options

**1. What Your Situation Involves:**
Based on what you've shared, this involves Defective product regarding ₹35,000.

**2. Applicable Legal Provisions:**
- **[The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 — Section 2(47)](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/15256)**: Unfair Trade Practice and Refusal to Take Back Defective Goods or Refund
- **[Consumer Protection (E-Commerce) Rules, 2020 — Rule 4 & Rule 6](https://consumeraffairs.nic.in/sites/default/files/E-commerce%20Rules.pdf)**: Duties of E-Commerce Entities & Grievance Redressal Mechanism
- **[The Payment of Wages Act, 1936 — Section 5 & Section 15](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/2405)**: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
- **[The Consumer Protection Act, 2019 — Section 2(7)](https://www.indiacode.nic.in/handle/123456789/15256)**: Definition of Consumer (Including E-commerce and Offline Purchases)
- Under Indian law, arbitrary retention of funds without verifiable itemized loss is legally unsustainable.
- In tenancy disputes, routine painting and standard aging fall under reasonable wear and tear (Transfer of Property Act, 1882 Section 108).
- In consumer matters, refusal to replace or refund for defective products is an Unfair Trade Practice under Section 2(47) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019.

**3. Practical Evidence to Preserve:**
- Bank/UPI payment receipts.
- Date-stamped photographs or handover videos.
- Written communications (WhatsApp/emails).

**4. Recommended Action:**
- Send a formal written demand notice with an explicit 15-day compliance window.
- If unresolved, proceed to pre-litigation conciliation via the National Consumer Helpline (1915), state Rent Authority, or Labour Commissioner.

citations.title: Unfair Trade Practice and Refusal to Take Back Defective Goods or Refund
citations.description: Refusing to take back or withdraw defective goods or to withdraw or discontinue deficient services and to refund the consideration contemplated within the period stipulated, or within 30 days if no period is stipulated, constitutes an unfair trade practice.

citations.title: Duties of E-Commerce Entities & Grievance Redressal Mechanism
citations.description: Every e-commerce entity shall establish an adequate grievance redressal mechanism and appoint a Grievance Officer whose details are displayed on its platform. The officer must acknowledge receipt within 48 hours and redress the complaint within one month.

citations.title: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.

citations.title: Definition of Consumer (Including E-commerce and Offline Purchases)
citations.description: Defines a consumer as any person who buys goods or hires/avails any services for a consideration paid or promised, including offline or online transactions through electronic means or by teleshopping or direct selling.
